text:
Cole Sillinger is 23, an alternate captain in Columbus, and playing about 16 minutes a night with a bigger physical game than ever: 44 hits in 20 games. He has 4 goals and 9 points, and his scoring rate is a touch better than last season's.

The five-on-five numbers aren't flattering. The Blue Jackets take about 46% of the expected goals with him on the ice, a little worse than without him. But they've also scored five fewer goals than their chances deserve while he's out there, and our numbers flag that as the kind of luck that usually swings back, which would help his assist total most.

There's a caution from last season too. Evolving-Hockey had his results running ahead of his chances and noted strong linemates flattering his raw numbers, so 2025-26 may have overstated him a little. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had nothing that stood out either way. His ice time is up more than a minute over his last ten games. Columbus has lost seven of those ten, and we'd watch whether that bigger role holds as the team looks for answers.
headline: Cole Sillinger is doing more than the points show
